title: Adaptive Export Scheduler for Cross-Backend Trace Compatibility
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement an Adaptive Export Scheduler that dynamically selects and configures trace exporters per-tenant and per-request to ensure compatibility with multiple backends (Tempo, Jaeger, legacy in-house collectors) while minimizing tail-latency and memory pressure. This scheduler will perform:

- schema translation mapping (remap legacy tags to OTLP semantic conventions)
- dynamic batching and envelope sizing per-backend
- per-tenant credential selection and rotation hooks
- fallbacks on backend congestion (queueing, degrade to sampling)
- lightweight enrichment for missing fields required by downstream backends

Scope: runtime component in trace-ingest pipeline (sidecar/relay), scheduler config UI in Console for operators, e2e perf tests. Not in scope: full rewrite of exporters; we will extend current exporter adapters with negotiation hooks.
comments: 2026-01-19 Maya Chen: Spike complete — validated core idea with a prototype scheduler in the trace-relay. Prototype supports per-tenant exporter selection and simple schema remapping rules. Baseline microbenchmarks show ~6% CPU increase and 12% added P50 processing latency under synthetic load (1k RPS). Recording details in confluence: https://confluence.redwood/inference/observability/adaptive-export-scheduler-spike

2026-01-22 Omar Ruiz: Design doc posted — details on negotiation API, rule DSL, and compatibility table for Tempo/Jaeger/legacy collectors: https://confluence.redwood/inference/observability/adaptive-export-scheduler-design. Requesting review from @Anika Bhandari (SRE) and @Liam Park (Runtime).

2026-01-25 Anika Bhandari (SRE): Review notes — need hard SLOs for scheduler to avoid head-of-line blocking. Suggest bounded queue per-exporter and circuit-breaker semantics. Also call out observability for dropped spans and backpressure signals (metric names proposed).

2026-01-28 Omar Ruiz: Implemented per-exporter bounded queues + circuit breaker. Added counters for exporter_queue_overflow and exporter_circuit_tripped. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-relay/pull/4124

2026-01-30 Maya Chen: Perf tests after queue change — CPU overhead reduced to ~3.5%, P95 latency increase limited to 18ms on worst path. Identified bug where credential rotation caused exporter handshake failure under burst; added retry/refresh backoff. Linked GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-relay/issues/4187

2026-02-01 Liam Park (Runtime): Code review done. Requested clearer tests around schema translation edge cases (nullable attributes, legacy trace-id formats). Also requested a feature flag for gradual rollout per-cluster. Omar to address before merging.

2026-02-02 Omar Ruiz: Added unit tests for schema translator (edge cases + round-trip), implemented cluster-scoped feature flag, and updated rollout playbook. Preparing canary plan targeting low-traffic tenants (see rollout checklist).

2026-02-02 Release engineer comment: Add Ops checklist item to run the dashboard query that compares exported span counts vs ingest counts — to detect silent drops during rollout. Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/instruments/d/trace-exports/exports-health
acceptance_criteria:
1) Scheduler can route spans to Tempo, Jaeger, and legacy collectors with mapping rules.
2) Circuit-breaker prevents unbounded memory growth under backend failures.
3) Per-tenant feature flag + Console toggle exists for rollout.
4) Perf regression <= 10% CPU and P95 increase <= 25ms in staging compared to baseline.
5) End-to-end tests and dashboard queries for export health are in place.
rollout_plan:
- Merge behind feature flag.
- Canary to 5 low-traffic tenants for 72h, monitor exporter_queue_overflow, exported_span_rate, and end-to-end error rate.
- If stable, incrementally enable per-cluster 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 7 days.
- If circuit-breaker tripped >5% of samples, rollback to previous binary and investigate.
follow_up_tasks: Add Console UI for exporter rule editor and per-tenant override
Add automated chaos test: simulate Tempo high-latency and observe graceful degradation
Audit existing exporters for idempotency and durable retry semantics
